claims.statement: Termind's native targets remain platform-specific in Debug and Release: TFM targets macOS 15.0 and TFI targets iOS 18.0 on iPhone/iPad, with TFI's macOS metadata not adding a desktop platform. Both select development cloud/push environments in Debug and production in Release; desktop enables Sandbox and Hardened Runtime. The six shared Termind frameworks are static libraries with SKIP_INSTALL and empty signing identities, not runtime hosts. TFI embeds TermindWidgets.appex and uses automatic signing without a target identity override; TFM selects Apple Development and embeds termind-mcp with CodeSignOnCopy. Signing and packaging settings do not redefine native runtime ownership.

On macOS, TermindApp is the composition root: it creates one SwiftData container, prepares persistence and Keychain-backed services, constructs sync/outbox/repository dependencies, and retains one AppModel in SwiftUI state; failure to open the local container terminates startup rather than substituting an empty store.

AppModel coordinates desktop services app-wide while WindowModel owns independently mutable workspaces, selection, sidebar and search; idempotent registration injects shared services and rejects closed owners without transferring workspace ownership. Native command sets use focused window/scene values for local actions instead of global selection.

The macOS main WindowGroup shows diagnosis consent when required; otherwise it creates a WindowModel per scene (or reuses screenshot demo window state) while injecting the same app model and SwiftData container. A separate externally driven authentication window shares app dependencies.

The desktop native coordinator registers window owners, consumes new-window/live-transfer requests and preserves restored geometry; its bridge establishes fullSizeContentView and a transparent titlebar before sizing and suppresses edited decoration. The close proxy honors native vetoes, guards reentrancy, saves theme edits and asks discard approval only for remaining unsaved theme drafts, not live workspaces; detach restores the original delegate.

Accepted macOS termination performs idempotent cleanup after theme-save/discard handling and pending-SFTP-edit confirmation, without a live-workspace confirmation; it empties and disconnects window workspaces with applicationTermination intent rather than marking window models closed, and replies after cleanup or a three-second fallback.

TermindIOSApp constructs a startup Result with XCTest-dependent assembly and passes it through a sendable scene-content closure. MobileStartupView installs the successful container and operation-confirmation renderer, gates native scene binding on diagnosis consent, or shows unavailable-store content on construction failure; MobileAppDelegate configures scenes and queues early discards.

MobileAppDependencies live assembly shares one logged RemoteConnectionCoordinator across workspace connections, metrics, the app coordinator and RemoteSessionTerminator; MobileAppModel also uses it for assistant host services, transfers, SSH preferences and agent forwarding. Testing uses in-memory mode with injectable platform, recovery, effects and termination services; default/convenience construction is not equivalent to the explicitly shared live assembly.

MobileAppModel owns app-wide persistence, shared libraries, sync, assistant, metrics, transfers and forwarding, and coordinates a registry of native-window workspace sessions rather than owning an interchangeable workspace pool; production persists Termind.store under Application Support, while in-memory/test modes omit production sync.

The mobile quick-action scene root waits for a persistent UIKit session ID and keys MobileBoundSceneRoot by it; the bound root creates and retains MobileSceneModel in a task outside view construction, and MobileRootView retains that scene model, reports its phase to the shared app, exposes a focused scene value, and provides sidebar-adaptable tabs with independent navigation stacks.

Mobile live workspaces and their descriptors belong to a persistent native-window workspace session: two windows opening the same Host create independent instances, while repeated selection in one owner session reuses its published instance and does not duplicate the initial connection attempt.

Mobile Live Activities project the successfully loaded authoritative saved/live workspace list, with dormant descriptors disconnected, rather than recovering entries from system cards. Restore preserves focus and retires duplicates; empty snapshots end cards, while failed snapshot reads leave cards untouched. Summaries exclude credentials/output, are bounded to six entries and 3500 bytes; serialized operations defer explicit starts and prevent ordinary updates from resurrecting dismissed cards.

Mobile background behavior aggregates scene phases and begins a finite task only when all tracked scenes background. Sync and monitoring pause; Mosh/ET suspend and checkpoint immediately, while expiry retires remaining workspace, forwarding, transfer and assistant work. Active scenes refresh device naming and resume eligible services. Device-local encrypted TerminalRecoveryStore checkpoints are independent of SwiftData/Vault/CloudKit: leases fence saves against close, consumption validates Host and transport/version and removes eligibility before returning counters. Missing checkpoints fail rather than bootstrap a replacement shell, except separate managed-session recovery can require selection without startup replay.

Desktop external SSH/SFTP/Telnet URL handling opens temporary unsaved workspace/session state in the target window; Telnet URLs that carry an advisory password require explicit confirmation before opening.

Connection-history event lifetime follows the saved-host workspace or pane: creation starts an event, explicit close ends it, desktop pane moves preserve it, and Serial or temporary connections are excluded.

Both app composition roots create an app-wide DeviceDirectoryModel with the Vault installation ID. macOS names it from trimmed kern.hostname with a DeviceKit fallback; iOS uses Device.current.safeDescription directly. Foreground activation refreshes the directory record without rewriting connection events.

Mobile reconcileSync starts or pauses Vault, History, Device, Metrics and Settings coordinators behind an active-scene and Pro gate; individual coordinator lifecycles additionally honor master/optional preferences. Sync changes invoke reconciliation, and the app-owned pro.accessDidChange callback reconciles sync, Tailscale, metrics and connection preferences independently of root-view mounting.

Desktop AppModel starts and reconciles five coordinators (Vault, connection History, Device, Metrics and Settings) with Pro access and no scene-phase gate; coordinators check the master switch and their applicable optional-category preferences.

A local mobile Host deletion closes associated saved and live workspaces, retires runtime dependencies, requests durable repository deletion, projects removal and starts the outbox; a failed request reports an error. Remote removal also prunes opened and unopened workspace descriptors, while route changes disconnect affected sessions without removing descriptors.

A desktop Host deletion request persists the repository deletion before projecting removal and clearing connection history; outbox handlers coordinate closing window-owned workspaces, canceling transfers and forwarding, clearing references and final removal. The SwiftData deletion marker and all outbox jobs are committed atomically for crash recovery.

Desktop shutdown fences assistant admission, cancels pending managed-session close tasks, stops notifications/badge, cancels preparations and stops conversations before awaiting persistence. MCP/SFTP drains run concurrently, followed by agent commands, pools and Tailscale. Window workspaces disconnect with applicationTermination intent preserving managed remote sessions; repeated calls share one task and the once-only fallback reply does not guarantee drains completed.

MobileBackgroundController owns one finite UIKit background-task lease at a time, retires a previous lease before beginning another, ignores stale expiration callbacks and retires the lease after expiration or foreground finish; an invalid task identifier triggers immediate expiration.

UIKit Home Screen quick actions are staged per MobileSceneDelegate and consumed once by the scene's MobileRootView; MobileSceneModel routes connect to the picker and recent-host actions through the Host's current preferred connection kind, reporting unavailable hosts rather than restoring a stale session.

Mobile Home Screen recent-host shortcut items are refreshed from local connection history when scene phase, history or host configuration changes and are limited to three openable recent Hosts; unknown and malformed shortcut payloads are rejected.

Removing a mobile scene triggers the all-scenes-background transition only if other tracked scenes remain and are all backgrounded; removing the last tracked scene or a backgrounded scene with another visible scene does not start a background lease.

MobileBackgroundController invokes its expiry callback synchronously before retiring a valid UIKit task, including when expiration occurs during begin; it safely retires the returned identifier without disturbing a replacement lease, while asynchronous cleanup initiated by expiration is best effort.

Mobile Mosh/ET transports suspend and checkpoint on all-scenes-background entry and resume the retained transport on foreground after invalidating its checkpoint. Other active connection flows detach on background-task expiry, clear interactive authentication and set foreground reconnect intent; only intent-bearing workspaces resume, preserving healthy ordinary connections on quick returns.

The macOS entrypoint sets up its scrubber client and captures launchLanguage before opening the container, then cleans old context attachments after open; screenshot launches return an isolated in-memory demo runtime. The captured locale is injected into main and authentication scenes; Settings stores changes for the next launch and displays a notice, without automatically relaunching or replacing the root locale.

In DEBUG XCTest launches the real macOS app with an in-memory container and test-isolated metrics defaults, no Vault, History, Device, Metrics or Settings cloud sync coordinators, disabled file logging, unrestricted Pro access, and no persisted default window size; database construction failure still triggers fatalError rather than resetting production data.

By default DEBUG XCTest suppresses automatic macOS main and authentication windows and disables restoration; setting TERMIND_WINDOW_TESTS=1 opts in to automatic windows but not restoration, while screenshot mode permits automatic launch and disables main-scene restoration. Dock reopening is blocked during suppression, the last closed fixture window cannot terminate the test host, and visible-window test suites are gated explicitly.

macOS Quit latches terminateLater, saves terminal-theme edits across registered windows and requests discard approval for remaining unsaved drafts before SFTP recheck and pending-edit confirmation. Veto resets the latch without shutdown, duplicate requests add no task, and the fallback starts only after acceptance; live workspaces do not themselves require Quit confirmation.

A macOS login launch configured to open quietly still creates its normal window and hides the app; a one-shot key-window observer with a three-second disarm prevents subsequent user-opened windows from being hidden.

RootView retains its per-scene WindowModel in SwiftUI state, registers it with AppModel on appearance and exposes it as a focused scene value. Restored native windows without a pending request preserve their system frame rather than replaying another window's move.
Both apps share CloudSyncSettingsContent with one aggregate status and optional History, Metrics, Settings switches in that order; Vault and Device have no separate toggle.

On mobile, a failed local Host deletion request does not project the Host removal or start the deletion outbox, but cleanup of live workspaces, assistant connections, edits, transfers, forwarding and metrics has already occurred and is not rolled back.

Mobile workspace links require an existing saved/live owner and activate that owner or materialize its descriptor under the same UUID; missing owners report unavailable. Activity links are UUID-only; legacy recovery-query parsing does not rebuild missing workspaces from URL or card metadata. External URLs remain temporary with Telnet password confirmation; notifications wait for active delivery and ignore superseded activation failures.

MobileWorkspaceStore retires legacy workspace/recently-closed keys and loads version-1 mobile.restorableWorkspaces.v1 snapshots grouped by native session ID without connecting. All saved descriptors are retained, not just resumable or managed SSH descriptors; missing-Host intent survives, external workspaces remain transient, and invalid snapshot reads fence writes against overwrite.

Mobile scene disconnect removes phase tracking without discarding ownership. UIKit discard of owners used in this process closes their descriptors/live workspaces and precisely tracked transferred workspaces without terminating managed remote sessions. Unbound cold-restored owners instead become recoverable orphans, so early or late archived-session discards do not erase their recovered records.

Mobile native-session reconciliation saves a complete ownership handoff snapshot before releasing sources, then transfers live objects, descriptor order and unread state and rewires callbacks without reconnecting or starting history events. Save failure preserves source ownership; absent targets wait. Multi-scene reconciliation preserves open owners, while single-window devices treat only the active session as reachable even when UIKit reports archived owners.

Outside XCTest the mobile app delegate registers for remote notifications at launch; on UIKit scene-session discard it closes sessions through the app model or queues their IDs until startup assigns that model.

Production macOS startup checks for a second nonterminated same-bundle application before opening its disk store, covering old app versions that did not acquire the store lock; an in-use error from either that preflight or container construction displays a database-in-use alert and exits on acknowledgment, while other startup errors are fatal.

On macOS, disk-backed SwiftData container creation acquires a nonblocking exclusive lock on a stable store lock file before open or migration, retains the lease through the container lifetime and shares it among same-process containers for the canonical store URL; in-memory containers do not contend and a different process gets an in-use error without opening the store.

Desktop commands register the main-window factory; UUID-valued requests retain layout and optional live Workspace/pane transfer until RootView's native bridge registers the NSWindow. A restored scene without a pending request keeps its system frame and does not replay a move.

The diagnostic data choice is installation-local and not a synced settings snapshot: production diagnosis controllers read local defaults, start reporting only for an existing affirmative choice, and permit the normal desktop/mobile root after either allowing or declining; inert screenshot and test controllers do not demand a choice.

TermindPersistence owns one versioned SwiftData schema and migration plan for both platforms; the platform entrypoints choose the store location or in-memory mode and retain the container, rather than defining separate platform model sets.
Memory-only app compositions disable Tailscale native profile storage and reject native node factory calls, preventing tests from accessing live device node state.

Mobile pushed detail and native search presentation have a shorter lifetime than session-owned Workspaces: switching details by workspace ID dismantles UIKit search, while queries, journey, connection and native terminal remain runtime-owned. Presentation teardown does not itself save descriptors or connect.

Passive native window dismissal preserves managed-session recovery references on both platforms; explicit workspace/pane closure instead immediately removes local state and queues eligible remote termination without a persistent-session close prompt. The app-wide RemoteSessionCloseCoordinator deduplicates identities, owns transferred cleanup connections independently, requests cancellation after a default 30-second deadline and releases connections after operation completion; enqueue does not guarantee remote success. Reopen avoids identities whose termination was enqueued, and mobile background expiration cancels pending close tasks.

Mobile required runtime/persistence construction errors propagate to the startup Result and unavailable-store UI without an empty-store fallback, whereas workspace snapshot read errors are caught inside MobileAppModel: construction succeeds with app.error, activity restoration is skipped, subsequent activity projection/start is gated off, and MobileWorkspaceStore fences writes.

The iOS applicationWillTerminate callback stops notification badge/observers/routing through clearNotificationBadge; it does not perform desktop-style coordinated asynchronous shutdown or discard workspace sessions. Mobile descriptor persistence and background checkpoint handling are separate lifecycle paths.
